identity.title: In-the-Flow Agentic System Optimization for Effective Planning and Tool Use

problem.claim: How to train agentic systems for effective long-horizon planning and tool use during live, multi-turn interaction.

gap.claim: Existing tool-augmented methods rely on monolithic policies that scale poorly and generalize weakly, while many modular systems are training-free or trained offline without live interaction dynamics.

contributions.claim: AgentFlow coordinates planner, executor, verifier, and generator modules through evolving memory, while optimizing the planner in the interaction loop.

Flow-GRPO converts multi-turn on-policy optimization into sequential single-turn updates for long-horizon, sparse-reward credit assignment, using trajectory-level outcome broadcasting and group-normalized advantages.
The authors report gains across search, agentic, mathematical, and scientific benchmark categories using a 7B-scale backbone.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present an in-the-flow, trainable agentic framework that directly optimizes planning within the live multi-turn loop.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, across ten benchmarks, AgentFlow exceeds their top-performing baselines by average accuracy gains of 14.9% on search, 14.0% on agentic, 14.5% on mathematical, and 4.1% on scientific tasks, and surpasses larger proprietary models such as GPT-4o.
The authors report analyses showing improved planning, more reliable tool calling, and positive scaling with model size and reasoning turns.

narrative_sequence.summary: The abstract identifies scaling, generalization, and live-interaction training limitations in existing approaches.
It introduces AgentFlow, a four-module system with evolving memory and in-the-flow planner optimization.
It proposes Flow-GRPO to make long-horizon, sparse-reward on-policy training tractable and align turn-level decisions with trajectory-level success.
The authors report category-level accuracy gains across ten benchmarks and favorable analyses of planning, tool calling, and scaling.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links local planner updates to a single verifiable trajectory-level outcome and uses group-normalized advantages to stabilize learning.

lessons.interpretation: This suggests a useful claim-to-evidence pattern: explicitly connect local decisions to the global objective while naming the mechanism that handles delayed feedback.
lessons.application: When presenting a multi-step training method, map each intermediate update to a shared end-to-end outcome and state how credit assignment is stabilized.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when intermediate actions have independently verifiable objectives or when no meaningful trajectory-level outcome exists.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify benchmark names, baseline identities, statistical uncertainty, or whether gains are statistically significant.
It does not provide ablation details isolating AgentFlow modules, Flow-GRPO components, or the reported scaling effects.
